task: Fix the single blocking finding from the final Biel4 review. Rust screen_vision_fixtures currently returns two synthetic fixtures plus every EnumDisplayMonitors result, while packages/contracts parseScreenVisionFixtures rejects arrays longer than three. Define one explicit bounded maximum for real monitors (use 16 displays plus the two synthetic fixtures, total 18 records unless a safer documented bound is justified), enforce it in Rust enumeration and TS parser, and document the bound in the Phase 11 spec/limitations. Add/update Rust and contract tests proving a multi-display array (at least four records) is accepted up to the bound and the next record is rejected; preserve real display metadata acceptance and forbidden pixel/durable-field rejection. Do not weaken capture/cancellation/privacy/Owner gates or change Phase 12/13. Run cargo fmt/check/clippy/full/focused, contracts typecheck/build/tests, desktop typecheck/tests/build, secrets scan and diff check. Commit the correction; do not push or publish.
constraints: Use the configured Biel4 App Server Executor in fast mode; no native subagents and no direct manual code edits outside the Executor.
The bound must be explicit and shared/documented so Rust and TypeScript cannot diverge; no unbounded monitor metadata.
Keep no continuous capture, network/upload, raw screenshot persistence, or weakened privacy/safe-mode/Owner/idempotency controls.
Do not modify Phase 12 Android or Phase 13 gateway behavior; do not push, merge, tag, release or deploy.

review_findings.title: Rust and TypeScript fixture bounds diverge
review_findings.details: The Rust provider enumerates all monitors and returns two synthetic fixtures plus each real display, but parseScreenVisionFixtures in packages/contracts/src/index.ts rejects arrays longer than three. A multi-monitor response therefore fails at the UI boundary. Define and enforce a shared explicit maximum (recommended 18 total: 2 synthetic + 16 displays) and add compatibility tests.
